strengths: Aligning LLVM IR with source code and generated comments addresses a concrete problem with an identifiable audience in program analysis and code representation learning. The anchored encoder and staged interpolation provide a plausible training approach.
The manuscript reports improvements across several tasks and datasets. Examples include DIRE accuracy of 33.41 versus RoBERTa’s 29.41, and summarization BLEU-4 of 34.36 versus GraphCodeBERT’s 32.43.
Component ablations, a CodeT5 extension, and qualitative examples broaden the investigation. The stated release of code, models, and processed datasets could facilitate reuse.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 evaluation definition. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify disjoint sets of 64/16/24 problem labels, whereas Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe supervised classification into 104 classes. Ordinary closed-set classification does not explain evaluation on unseen labels. If this is retrieval, specify the training objective, candidate sets, and ranking metrics; otherwise explain a valid classification protocol. This ambiguity also affects the central ablation and CodeT5 results.

Necessary: Restrict the binary-analysis claims to the evaluated representation or provide supporting experiments. The inputs are compiler-generated LLVM IR, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function names and types. This does not establish performance on stripped executables or IR recovered from them. The footnote asserting trivial interchangeability is inaccurate. Evaluation on such inputs would support broader claims; a clearly scoped LLVM IR study could also satisfy TMLR’s criteria.

Necessary: Clarify evaluation partitions and model selection. Section 3.2 explicitly places generation evaluation on the validation set, while Section 4.3 refers to a test set. Distinguish pretraining partitions from downstream partitions and identify which selected checkpoints and which produced the reported scores. Document overlap handling and the provenance of summarization references, including whether they are CodeT5-generated. These omissions prevent a confident assessment of generalization.

Necessary for the component claims: Separate interpolation effects from additional training. PCL receives 10 pretraining epochs, while the full model receives 30 or 70. Section 5.1 asserts PCL convergence but supplies no convergence evidence or matched-budget comparison. Removing both interpolation stages together also does not establish their individual contributions or the benefit of their order. Provide appropriate controls or limit the conclusion to the complete training recipe.

Necessary: Qualify the comment-quality finding. Table 7 reports POJ-104 MAP of 3.11 with human comments, 42.76 without comments, and 43.78 with generated comments. This striking collapse warrants a documented extraction/alignment protocol and checks for training instability. The comparison confounds authorship with annotation purpose, length, and preprocessing. One classification experiment does not establish the broader comprehension claims in the abstract or general inferiority of human-written comments.

Necessary: Calibrate claims about semantic correctness and consistent superiority. BLEU, GLEU, and exact match measure textual agreement; they do not establish functional equivalence or preservation of long-range semantics. Figure 7 even gives GraphCodeBERT’s semantically comparable summary, 'Unloads the mutex,' against ContraBin’s 'Unloads a mutex.' Table 6 shows mixed results: ContraBin has lower BLEU than GraphCodeBERT and only a 0.43-point exact-match advantage. Add semantic validation and uncertainty estimates for stronger claims, or restrict conclusions to the observed metric differences.

Necessary clarification: Identify the actual implementation unambiguously. Equations 8 and 10 use summed embeddings, while Figure 3 illustrates concatenation; Algorithm 1 permits arbitrary modality pairs, whereas Section 2.4 describes source/comment interpolation. Specify the implemented choices and whether gradients pass through the binary-dependent targets in Equation 5. These choices affect the optimization and reproducibility.

Optional improvements: Simplify the repeated human-learning analogies and improve the readability of the case-study figures. Comparisons with binary- or IR-specific baselines would strengthen positioning, but neither a new method nor state-of-the-art performance is required for acceptance.
